# Local decoder patch

This copy comes from the crates.io `zune-jpeg` 0.5.15 package. Its package metadata identifies upstream commit `31d81fed7551c8ccea456d9d8e2b1fd8bebb6995`, path `crates/zune-jpeg`, in <https://github.com/etemesi254/zune-image>. Original source headers and MIT, Apache-2.0 and Zlib license files are retained.

The strict entropy-validation changes affect `src/bitstream.rs`, `src/mcu.rs` and `src/mcu_prog.rs`. The bitstream separately counts real entropy bits and records consumption of synthetic marker/EOF padding. Strict sequential and progressive decode paths reject that consumption; sequential decoding also rejects a marker that terminates an incomplete MCU row. Restart resets discard buffered padding but never erase an already detected violation. Lookahead may still use zeros without consuming them as coefficients, and permissive decoding behavior remains available to non-strict callers.

The workspace patch applies to both Picoli and its transitive image dependency. It does not modify the machine's shared Cargo registry. This is a local patch, not a claim that upstream has published the fix. Integration coverage lives in `picoli-core` and includes the original formerly ignored regression, scan truncation, valid final padding, odd dimensions, grayscale, three chroma sampling modes, progressive scans and restart markers.

The default-off `experimental-coefficients` feature also adds bounded quantized-coefficient capture and access in `src/coefficients.rs`, with integration into the decoder. `src/coefficients/renderer.rs` and `src/coefficients/chroma_renderer.rs` add local luma and chroma block-rendering interfaces for candidate evaluation. They reuse the decoder's existing IDCT, chroma upsampling and color conversion; those upstream algorithms are not Picoli inventions. The local interfaces check coefficient arithmetic bounds, support patch evaluation and preserve exact agreement with full decoding for the supported layouts.

Under `experimental-coefficients`, `stream_reconstruct_progressive` and the reusable `StreamReconstructor` additionally stream dequantization, IDCT, chroma upsampling, and YCbCr-to-RGB color conversion MCU-row-by-MCU-row directly from caller-provided quantized coefficient planes (with per-MCU-row preparation and early-exit callbacks), matching the full decoder output bit-for-bit without running entropy decoding/encoding for rejected quality candidates. `ChromaRenderer` also adds `swap_block`/`restore_block` for reversible paired trials without repeated IDCT and a direct 4:4:4 rectangle path matching the general renderer bit-for-bit.
